Romania’s Steel Sector Hit by Deepening Credit Freeze as Firms Face Plant Closures

Romania’s steel industry is facing a deepening financial crisis after a rapid credit freeze this month left some of the country’s largest producers and mills unable to secure short-term funding or refinance maturing debt. The turmoil, triggered by a wave of lender withdrawals and rising risk premiums, has already forced two major steelmaking sites to suspend operations, with local union representatives warning of potential layoffs affecting thousands of workers.

The situation escalated last week when Siderom SA, one of the country’s leading steel producers, announced a halt to output at its Galati plant after failing to secure a critical bridge loan. “We have exhausted all available lines of credit,” said Siderom CEO Mircea Albu in a statement. “The abrupt withdrawal of financing has left us no choice but to idle production lines until conditions stabilize.” Siderom employs over 2,400 staff at its Galati facility.

Industry association UniSteel Romania estimates that at least four other mills are operating at reduced capacity, with smaller firms especially vulnerable. “The entire sector is under severe pressure,” said UniSteel president Ana-Maria Petrescu. “If the credit freeze persists, we risk a cascade of plant shutdowns and significant job losses across the industry.”

Steel prices in Romania have fallen nearly 18% since the start of the quarter, intensifying the cash flow problems facing producers. The National Union of Steelworkers reported that over 1,300 workers have already been placed on temporary leave, with more at risk if the credit squeeze continues. “Our members are anxious about their future and demand urgent intervention to protect jobs,” said union leader Valentin Stan.

The Ministry of Industry has convened crisis talks with sector leaders but has yet to announce any support measures. The credit crisis remains ongoing, with industry executives warning that prolonged instability could reshape Romania’s steel landscape for years to come.
